A1.justification: Both PDFs describe villa-X and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable matching of methods, tables, figures, and appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original villa-X experiments on SIMPLER, LIBERO, Realman, and Xhand, together with ablations, probing results, and qualitative demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation and real-robot results, including the supplementary visualizations and evaluation details.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same latent action model, proprioceptive forward dynamics supervision, and jointly trained latent-action and robot-action diffusion components.

E1.justification: The training mixture in Table 6 and evaluation coverage remain unchanged: SIMPLER, four LIBERO suites, Realman manipulation, and Xhand tasks, including the same generalization scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces the SIMPLER GR00T comparator with GR00T-N1.5. MoTo, LAPA, and the other comparators remain; GR00T is also retained in the real-robot comparisons in Tables 4–5.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, trial counts, preprocessing, and training budgets are unchanged. Beyond identifying the replacement comparator, v2 documents no revised SIMPLER evaluation or fine-tuning procedure in Appendix D.1.

E4.justification: The proprioceptive-supervision probing, latent-action ablations, LAPA-style/Go-1-style comparisons, transfer visualizations, and real-world generalization analyses are retained without changes.

E5.justification: The repetition and trial information in Appendices D–E is unchanged. Neither version adds confidence intervals, seed-based variability estimates, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces GR00T's Google/WidowX averages of 1.4%/3.8% with GR00T-N1.5 results of 44.5%/62.0%; these are different comparators, not a same-model performance gain. GR00T-N1.5 takes the Carrot lead at 54.3%. Villa-X remains at 59.6%/62.5%, and all other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of latent actions, sequence lengths, and conditioning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: improved latent-action learning, improved incorporation into policy learning, and superior simulation and real-robot performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of alignment, transfer, planning, and policy gains remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitation concerning underexplored latent planning and the proposed future critic-based trajectory selection.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, preprocessing instructions, and resource links are unchanged. Appendix D.1 still gives the same generic GR00T checkpoint and fine-tuning description, without new N1.5-specific details.

R1.justification: Section 4.4.1 now positions GR00T-N1.5 as joint policy learning and world modeling using future embedding targets, separately from MoTo and LAPA's latent-action category. Section 2 and the bibliography remain unchanged, including reference [53]'s GR00T N1 title.

P1.justification: The SIMPLER baseline paragraph receives a localized rewrite introducing a separate world-modeling category. The remaining prose, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged apart from minor typographic spacing.

P2.justification: Table 2 removes a baseline-group separator and updates winner highlighting, while the additional baseline bullet causes limited page reflow. All figures and other table structures remain in place.

improvement.justification: The replacement SIMPLER comparator makes the comparison more informative: GR00T-N1.5's 62.0% WidowX average reveals how narrow villa-X's unchanged 62.5% lead is. Separating its modeling approach also improves the comparison's framing. The benefit is limited because the method and other evidence are unchanged, and the appendix and reference do not clarify the N1.5-specific setup.
